newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tokyo up slightly as Asia markets await Fed.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo up slightly as Asia markets await Fed.

text.p: Tokyo stocks moved marginally higher on Tuesday after a holiday break, but as with most Asian markets, trade was subdued ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting scheduled for later in the day.

Caution on a possible interest rate hike after the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting trimmed 0.65 percent from Hong Kong's key Hang Seng index, but Bangkok's bourse bounced back on optimism over a rumoured successor as prime minister.
Tokyo's key Nikkei 225 average closed up 59.75 points, or 0.28 percent, at 21,171.99. December futures were down 20 points to close at 21,160.
Brokers in Tokyo, which was closed for a national holiday on Monday, said most participants were sidelined not only by the FOMC meeting but because it was the last trading day for September delivery.

"People were reluctant to move much on the last trading day (for stock delivery within September) ahead of the end of the financial half-year. We'll also have the FOMC meeting tonight," said Hiroshi Morimoto, general manager at Daiwa Securities.
Hong Kong stocks ended near session lows, the Hang Seng 75.43 points lower at 11,546.70 after falling to 11,538.76.
"I think people are still waiting for the FOMC meeting tonight," said Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities.
Analysts said investors had discounted a 25 basis point rise in interest rates at the Fed meeting, and a hike could remove the uncertainty about interest rates in the market.
"But sentiment depends on whether (Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan says anything else after the rate hike. People are waiting for a message," said Chan.

Thai stocks gained 0.76 percent despite several bouts of profit taking after investors bought shares on rumours that former premier Chatichai Choonhavan might become prime minister again, brokers said.
The SET index, which hit its intraday low at 1,021.20 at the lunch break, rose after the market resumed in the afternoon session and ended 7.84 points higher at 1,042.21.
"Investors gained more confidence after the rumours spread in the market that Chatichai would become the new prime minister," said Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities.

Chatichai, now leader of the opposition Chart Pattana Party, was seen as a compromise candidate to replace outgoing premier Banharn Silpa-archa, brokers said. Banharn said on Saturday he would step down in seven days after choosing a successor.
Seoul shares closed higher after investors focused on major blue chips, brokers said. The index rose 8.71 points or 1.13 percent to provisionally close at 777.91.
The Australian share market gained ground, with the All Ordinaries index up 9.5 points or 0.43 percent at 2228.7.
Brokers said bargain hunters had buoyed the bourse after an initial selldown, driven by weaker metals prices overnight, quickly petered out and investors went looking for value.

Singapore's key share index finished flat as investors stayed on the sidelines ahead of the FOMC meeting. The key Straits Times Industrials Index rose a marginal 3.48 points, or 0.16 percent, to 2,160.27.
Caution also prevailed on Jakarta's bourse, the Composite Index ending 0.4 points, or 0.07 percent, at 569.77 points.
Philippine shares finished lower with trading mostly in speculative shares, traders said. The main index slipped by 8.06 points, or by 0.25 percent, to 3,236.48 points.
At 1126 GMT, the dollar was at 109.74/9.79 yen and 1.5126/32 marks.
Bullion ended at US$381.50/382.00, against New York's US$381.50/382.00 close on Monday.
SIMEX Brent crude oil futures for November were slightly firmer in late trading. November Brent last tarded at $22.30 a barrel, up four cents from London's settle of $22.26.
